Summary Description: Greg Muller is a leading figure in the algebraic and geometric study of cluster algebras and their interactions with noncommutative algebra, Poisson geometry, and representation theory. His work emphasizes explicit, constructive approaches to deep problems: establishing finite global dimensions for endomorphism-ring constructions End_R(A) associated to conic modules on toric algebras, deriving explicit projective resolutions of simple End_R(A)-modules, and characterizing when End_R(A) yields noncommutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) in relation to simplicial geometry. He has advanced the Poisson-geometry side of cluster algebras through the study of GSV Poisson structures on upper cluster algebras and the analysis of Azumaya loci for root-of-unity quantum cluster algebras, linking central subalgebras to classical upper cluster algebras. In addition, he co-authored foundational work on the superunitary region of cluster algebras, establishing a CW-structure and a tight correspondence with generalized associahedra in finite type, and contributed to theta-function theory in cluster algebras via scattering diagrams, valuations, and reciprocity theorems. Across these themes, his research blends combinatorial, homological, geometric, and topological methods to illuminate the structure and representations of cluster- and toric-algebraic objects, often via seed-data formalisms, dualities, and geometric interpretations on surfaces and moduli spaces.
